# AI Agent Instructions for this Repository

This repository is a static Jekyll blog site for GitHub Pages.

## What to edit
- Source content is in:
  - `_posts/` for dated blog posts
  - `pages/` for standalone site pages
  - `_wiki/` for wiki content
  - `post_bark/` for legacy/post archive content
- Layout and templates are in:
  - `_layouts/`
  - `_includes/`
- Static assets are in:
  - `css/`
  - `images/`
- The root `index.html` is a Jekyll homepage template.

## What not to edit directly
- `_site/` is generated site output. Do not modify it by hand.
- `.jekyll-cache/` is also generated.

## Build and preview
- Primary build command: `jekyll build`
- Local preview: `jekyll serve`
- If a Gemfile is added later, use `bundle exec jekyll build` and `bundle exec jekyll serve`.

## Repository conventions
- `/_config.yml` is the main Jekyll configuration.
- Permalinks are configured as `/:year/:month/:day/:title/`.
- Posted markdown files in `_posts/` should use the Jekyll post filename format: `YYYY-MM-DD-title.md`.
- `_wiki/` pages are published under `/wiki/:path/`.
- `feed.xml`, `sitemap.xml`, and site metadata are generated by plugins listed in `_config.yml`.

## Useful guidance for AI agents
- Focus changes on source files and templates, not the generated `_site/` output.
- Preserve existing front matter and formatting for blog posts.
- When adding or editing content, keep markdown structure consistent with surrounding files.
- There is no detected npm, Python, or Java project configuration in this repository.

## Notes
- This is a content-focused static site, not an application with automated tests in the repository.
- If build problems arise, check that Jekyll and the required plugins (`jekyll-paginate`, `jekyll-sitemap`, `jekyll-feed`) are installed.
